newsitem.title: FINLAND: CULTOR SAYS SOLVAY DEAL DELAY FOUR MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: CULTOR SAYS SOLVAY DEAL DELAY FOUR MONTHS.

text.p: Finnish food and biotechnology group Cultor Oy said on Monday its part-purchase of enzymes activities from Solvay was delayed by four months by a hold-up in clearance from U.S. authorities.

"The acquisition was supposed to be cleared by the end of March, but due to a delay in the clearance process it was approved early in July," Cultor spokeswoman Raija Kariola told Reuters. "So we are some four months behind the schedule in taking over the unit," she said.
Cultor said earlier the purchase, by its Genencor joint venture with Eastman Chemical Co, had been delayed.
Kariola said Cultor had not uncovered any surprises in the business and the takeover would mainly involve eliminating overlapping areas between two organisations.
"We have to examine synergies," she said.
Kariola also said a profit forecast given by Cultor in its Monday statement, which warned against overly optimistic expectations, was in line with forecasts Cultor has given earlier this year.

Cultor said in the statement it had already expected a "somewhat lower" result. But in its latest outlook at a June news conference, Cultor CEO Bjorn Mattson said earnings per share would stay close to the 1995 level.
Cultor's stock, which has risen significantly this year and solidly outperformed the HEX general share index, on Monday fell after the company's outlook statement.
At 1630/1330 GMT, Cultor's 1-series share traded at 209.30 markka, down 15.70 markka or some seven percent, but trade was modest. Cultor's usually more liquid 2-series was untraded.
